dimensions.assessment: Directly affects Department of State personnel, federal interagency partners involved in Arctic policy, and diplomatic relations with Arctic nations.
dimensions.evidence: there is authorized within the Department of State an Ambassador-at-Large for Arctic Affairs

dimensions.assessment: Creates a new high-level diplomatic position and formalizes an Arctic Region Security Policy and reporting framework, without altering domestic legal rights or civilian populations directly.
dimensions.evidence: Facilitate the development and coordination of United States foreign policy and programs in the Arctic region

dimensions.assessment: Authorizes a new diplomatic office and ongoing reporting requirements, though specific funding levels are not stated.
Amends the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 to establish the ambassador role and outline specific duties and security policy coordination.
dimensions.evidence: Title I of the State Department Basic Authorities Act of 1956 (22 U.S.C. 2651a et seq.) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent diplomatic office, while certain reporting requirements include a 10-year sunset provision.
dimensions.evidence: The reporting requirement in this section shall expire on the date that is 10 years after the date of the enactment of this Act

missing_information: Exact fiscal costs for establishing and staffing the Ambassador's office and supporting diplomatic missions.
importance_detail.rationale: Establishes a Senate-confirmed Ambassador-at-Large for Arctic Affairs within the State Department and mandates regular interagency reporting on Arctic security and foreign influence, primarily affecting diplomatic operations.
